scores.rationale: Broadly substrate-upward (infra → pipelines → deploy → migration), but observability comes after migration and deployment infra follows pipelines, so dependencies are not proven before use.

scores.evidence: Pilot Services (3-5 services) in Phase 5, Weeks 12-20
scores.rationale: No thin end-to-end prod slice first; the first pilot is after 11 weeks of horizontal layers.

scores.evidence: Select CI/CD platform (Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, ArgoCD)
scores.rationale: Options are listed without defaults or flip conditions; irreversible choices are not flagged.

scores.evidence: Batch 1: Pilot Services... Low-risk, well-understood services
scores.rationale: Migration batches ordered from low-risk pilots to complex ones, and platform before services, but no explicit widest-impact-first ordering within phases.
Secrets and scanning appear in Phases 2-3, but security hardening and compliance are trailing in Phases 7 and 9, and not in every phase.
Observability is scheduled mid-plan after migration begins, not from day zero, despite a passing 'DORA metrics from the start' remark.
IaC, Dockerfile standards and environment parity appear but late and not threaded through every phase.

scores.evidence: Automated rollbacks; Disaster recovery testing; Failover mechanisms
scores.rationale: Rollbacks and HA appear in Phases 4, 7 and 9, mostly late, not threaded from the start.
Plan never addresses whether an AI layer applies, so there is no N/A declaration.
No explicit list of deferred work with pull-forward conditions; only a vague 'Pilot Success' gate between batches.

note: A conventional horizontal-layer waterfall plan. It has no walking skeleton, no decision gates and no early observability, and it never addresses the AI question.
